key_insight: Fine-tuned generative models (DreamBooth on Stable Diffusion) can produce synthetic paintings that, when combined with real artworks, measurably improve authorship attribution accuracy and generalization under limited-data conditions.
problem_solved: Overcomes the scarcity of labeled paintings for training classifiers by augmenting datasets with high-fidelity, artist-specific synthetic images to improve model learning and robustness.
method: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion with DreamBooth per artist to generate synthetic paintings capturing stylistic cues.
Create hybrid training sets that combine real artworks and synthetic images to train attribution classifiers.
Evaluate classification accuracy and generalization across similar artists/styles to quantify gains from synthetic augmentation.
impact: Provides a practical pipeline for AI practitioners to expand scarce art datasets and boost attribution performance without needing large collections of real works. This approach generalizes to other low-data visual attribution problems where style preservation matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: DreamBooth fine-tuning → synthetic painting generation → hybrid dataset → classifier
Bar chart: classification accuracy comparison (real-only vs. synthetic-only vs. hybrid)
Embedding plot (t-SNE/UMAP): feature separation improves with synthetic augmentation
Gallery: side-by-side examples of real vs. synthetic paintings for several artists
paper_title: Enhancing Authorship Attribution with Synthetic Paintings
paper_authors: Clarissa Loures, Caio Hosken, Luan Oliveira, Gianlucca Zuin, Adriano Veloso
